name: House
description: Warm, communal dance music driven by a steady, buoyant heartbeat kick that makes the chest thud and hips sway. Radiant piano chords and uplifting human voices interlock over crisp handclaps to create a joyous, sweat-drenched warehouse party.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Steady, bouncing four-beat bass drum thump accompanied by sharp off-beat hissing hats (120-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm electronic piano chords, bouncy synthesized basslines, rhythmic handclaps, and analog drum machines
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Soulful, passionate human voices delivering soaring, gospel-infused affirmations or hypnotic spoken phrases
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Uplifting, communal, hedonistic, and emotionally warm

distinctionNotes: Unlike Techno, which is mechanical, cold, and repetitive, House relies on soulful human warmth, bright piano chords, and swung, bouncing grooves.

name: Techno
description: Hypnotic, machine-driven electronic music built from looping, metallic pulses that feel like standing inside an operating factory floor. Stripped of traditional melodies, it creates a trance-like state through subtle shifts in grating textures and hollow subterranean rumbles.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Relentless, heavy clockwork march with an unyielding mechanical kick (125-135 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Hissing industrial machinery, cycling synthesizer pulses, alien bleeps, and resonant metallic clicks
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Rare to nonexistent; occasional ghostly, detached vocal snippets or robotic spoken mantras
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Dark, futuristic, cavernous, and intensely hypnotic

distinctionNotes: Unlike House, which celebrates human warmth and organic soul, Techno is stark, synthetic, and architectural, emphasizing endless mechanical cycles over vocal hooks.

name: Synthwave / Outrun
description: Cinematic, retro-futuristic synthesizer music that captures the feeling of speeding down a palm-lined highway toward a neon sunset in an imagined 1980s film. Gleaming synthesized brass and shimmering arpeggios float over punchy, echoing drum-machine beats.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Steady, driving mid-tempo beat with snappy, booming snare hits wrapped in giant cavernous echoes (85-115 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Bright analog synthesizer brass, soaring electric lead melodies, bubbling basslines, and glistening electric guitar solos
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Airy, smooth 80s-style pop crooning, heavily filtered through radio static, or completely instrumental
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Nostalgic, romantic, cinematic, and saturated with neon melancholy

distinctionNotes: Unlike modern EDM or House, Synthwave deliberately emulates the gated-reverb drums, warm analog poly-synths, and cinematic soundtrack moods of the mid-to-late 1980s.

name: Drum & Bass
description: High-velocity electronic music driven by lightning-fast, syncopated drum breaks and deep, earth-quaking sub-bass that vibrates through the floor. The music combines rapid kinetic energy with expansive, atmospheric synth pads to evoke an urban speed run.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Extremely fast, staggered two-step drum pattern driven by sharp, slicing snare hits (170-178 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Deep chest-rattling sub-bass rumbles, manipulated acoustic drum loops, swelling synthesizer chords, and sci-fi laser sweeps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Soulful, floating female vocal loops or rapid-fire MC chants emphasizing rhythmic momentum
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Frenetic, technologically sophisticated, adrenaline-fueled, and urban

distinctionNotes: Unlike Dubstep, which operates at a half-time swagger, Drum & Bass moves at breakneck speeds, driven by tumbling, rolling snare patterns rather than robotic mid-bass drops.

name: Dubstep
description: Heavy, spacious bass music propelled by an unhurried, swaying stomp and overwhelming tectonic sub-frequencies that you feel in your marrow. Built on dramatic pauses, the music balances deep empty silence with shuddering, aggressive walls of low-end pressure.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Half-time swaggering rhythm where the heavy snare lands strictly once every two beats (typically 140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Monstrously heavy sub-bass waves, metallic scrape sounds, cavernous echo drops, and cracking wood-block snares
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Eerie, pitch-shifted, disembodied vocal murmurs washed out in endless dub delay
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Brooding, nocturnal, spatially expansive, and physically pulverizing

distinctionNotes: Unlike Drum & Bass, Dubstep half-times its pulse to create a lumbering, heavyweight swagger with vast expanses of eerie negative space between beats.

name: Ambient / Downtempo
description: Drifting, weightless electronic music made of vast sonic landscapes, gentle textural hiss, and slow-breathing harmonic clouds. It removes the pressure of the dance floor, allowing the listener to float through tranquil, timeless sound baths.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Completely rhythm-less and floating, or anchored by an unhurried, gentle, cushioned beat (60-90 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Vast synthesizer washes, field recordings of wind or water, delicate warm piano notes, and soft tape crackle
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Wordless angelic vocal hums, faint whispered fragments, or completely voice-free
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Tranquil, meditative, melancholic, and boundless

distinctionNotes: Unlike standard club genres designed to provoke immediate physical dancing, Ambient/Downtempo suppresses driving percussion to explore architectural acoustic space and psychological calm.

name: Deep House
description: Velvety, intimate house music characterized by warm electric piano chords, silky basslines, and late-night lounge sophistication. It trades peak-time energy for an intoxicating, understated groove that wraps around the listener like soft smoke.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Muffled, gentle four-to-the-floor kick with a relaxed, deeply swung rhythmic shuffle (118-124 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm Fender Rhodes electric piano chords, muted jazz organ tones, rounded sub-bass, and organic shaker percussion
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Sensual, hushed spoken word poetry or soulful, breathy vocal improvisations sitting deep in the mix
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Intimate, sultry, reflective, and subterranean

distinctionNotes: Unlike Tech House, which uses piercing, dry metallic percussion and functional club builds, Deep House relies on warm jazz chords, muted acoustics, and meditative soul.

name: Acid House
description: Hypnotic, hallucinatory dance music driven by a signature squealing, squelching synthesizer line that morphs and bubbles like boiling liquid. Its relentless rhythmic pulse and dizzying frequency sweeps produce an ecstatic, disorienting trance state.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Staccato, driving four-on-the-floor kick propelled by clicking, tinny hi-hats (122-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: The iconic squealing, resonant, rubbery squelch of the Roland TB-303 synthesizer paired with dry vintage drum machine snaps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Minimal, warped, repeated vocal phrases manipulated with wild delays or ecstatic chants
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Trippy, euphoric, chaotic, and chemically charged

distinctionNotes: Distinguished instantly from regular House by the prominent, shape-shifting, squealing Roland TB-303 bass synth that constantly twists its filter resonance into screaming, liquid shrieks.

name: Tech House
description: Lean, muscular club music that blends the clean, punchy drive of house with the cold, sterile percussion of techno. It features short, catchy bass loops and snappy drum hits designed to produce an unceasing, addictive physical groove.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Punchy, prominent four-on-the-floor kick with crisp, tight wooden claps and driving snare rolls (124-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Short percussive sub-bass bounces, sterile white-noise whooshes, dry metallic bleeps, and processed cowbells
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Quirky, pitched-down, spoken-word one-liners or chopped vocal loops used as rhythmic instruments
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: High-energy, functional, sleek, and laser-focused on the dancefloor

distinctionNotes: Unlike Deep House's emotional warmth, Tech House strips away soulful melodies in favor of a sterile, rubbery bassline and repetitive, hard-edged percussive drive.

name: French Touch / Nu-Disco
description: Glamorous, high-energy dance music constructed around sparkling 1970s disco samples that sweep dramatically through warm underwater filters before exploding into euphoric climaxes. It feels like dancing under a blinding mirror ball while champagne corks pop.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Pumping, sidechained four-on-the-floor beat where the entire track ducks and breathes with the kick drum (120-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Thick funky electric slap bass, filtered brass loops, sparkling disco string samples, and phaser-drenched synth sweeps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Cheerfully robotic vocoder melodies or pitch-shifted disco diva loops singing infectious hooks
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Flamboyant, celebratory, sunlit, and gloriously stylish

distinctionNotes: Unlike purist House, this style relies on recognizable, swept-frequency vintage disco samples, aggressive sidechain volume ducking, and metallic vocoder vocals.

name: Industrial / Peak Time Techno
description: A punishing, relentless sonic assault driven by distorted, hammer-like bass drums that sound like steel beams pounding against concrete. Cavernous metallic reverberations and howling siren synths evoke a high-pressure, dark warehouse raved to exhaustion.

benchmarkTracks.title: Look What Your Love Has Done To Me

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Ferocious, heavily overdriven four-on-the-floor kick drum thumping at relentless speeds (132-145 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Distorted screeching synth feedback, clanging sheet-metal hits, overdriven sub-bass rumbles, and harsh white-noise blasts
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Aggressive, distorted shouts, cold military commands, or completely non-vocal
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Brutal, apocalyptic, suffocating, and adrenaline-charged

distinctionNotes: Unlike Minimal or Melodic Techno, Industrial Techno uses extreme overdrive and distortion on its kick drums, creating an abrasive, physically punishing wall of noise.

name: Melodic Techno
description: Dramatic, cinematic techno that pairs a stern, thumping kick drum with sweeping, tragic synthesizer melodies that build to emotional breaking points. Evokes flying through a vast, starry digital cosmos filled with ancient mechanical monoliths.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Steady, driving four-on-the-floor beat wrapped in deep, warm sub-bass pulses (122-126 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Cascading, arpeggiated sawtooth synthesizers, cinematic orchestral pads, dramatic snare builds, and cavernous reverbs
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Ethereal, haunting, operatic vocal phrases drifting in wide acoustic spaces
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Grandiose, melancholic, epic, and emotionally transcendent

distinctionNotes: Unlike Peak Time Techno's raw, abrasive violence, Melodic Techno prioritizes sweeping minor-key musical story arcs, emotional synthesizer arpeggios, and vast cinematic spaces.

name: Minimal Techno
description: Skeletal, clinical electronic music stripped down to the barest microscopic clicks, muted thumps, and echoing hollow pops. It creates a surgical, hypnotic groove where every tiny ping of sound reverberates across vast empty silence.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Dry, clinical, unadorned kick drum marching through an austere grid (124-130 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Subtle sub-bass pulses, skeletal clicking percussion, glitchy static snaps, and muted metallic resonances
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Virtually nonexistent, save for occasional dry, chopped-up syllables treated as percussive clicks
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sterile, microscopic, meditative, and starkly architectural

distinctionNotes: Unlike Peak Time or Melodic Techno, Minimal systematically deletes chord pads, melodies, and heavy reverb, maintaining a skeletal acoustic landscape dominated by negative space.

name: Liquid DnB
description: Smooth, soulful drum and bass where high-speed tumbling breakbeats glide effortlessly over lush electric piano chords and warm, liquid bass swells. It feels like rushing weightlessly through a glowing metropolis at midnight.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Fast, rolling, aerodynamic breakbeat with crisp, light snare snaps (170-175 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Deep, smooth Sine-wave basslines, jazz guitar licks, shimmering Rhodes chords, and sweeping string textures
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Silky, emotionally rich soul and R&B vocal melodies floating effortlessly across the mix
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Breezy, melancholic, elegant, and uplifting

distinctionNotes: Unlike aggressive Neurofunk, Liquid DnB avoids distorted, gnarly basslines, substituting warm jazz harmonies, soul vocals, and a light, fluid atmosphere.

name: Neurofunk
description: Dark, hyper-technical drum and bass featuring snarling, mechanical basslines that twist and tear like violent robotic creatures. Its razor-sharp drum engineering and dystopian sci-fi aesthetic create a claustrophobic, high-threat sonic landscape.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Surgical, hyper-compressed two-step drum beats with cracking, whip-like snares (172-178 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Grotesque, morphing 'Reese' basslines, mechanical grinding textures, complex digital distortions, and icy laser hits
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Sparse, menacing cybernetic vocal samples or deep, ominous spoken warnings
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Dystopian, clinical, predatory, and brutally aggressive

distinctionNotes: Distinguished from Liquid DnB and Jungle by its complex, snarling, heavily modulated digital bass design and cold, hyper-precise sci-fi sound effects.

name: Jungle
description: Raw, rhythmically complex street music powered by chopped, tumbling acoustic drum breaks that stutter and crash over deep, vibrating reggae basslines. It crackles with Jamaican sound-system energy, sirens, and rapid vocal shouts.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Complex, syncopated, violently chopped acoustic breakbeats (particularly the 'Amen break') darting at high speeds (160-170 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Earth-shaking reggae dub sub-bass, vinyl scratches, gunshot sound effects, and air-raid sirens
sensoryHallmarks.voice: High-energy Jamaican dancehall toasting, reggae chants, and sped-up soulful vocal cries
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Rowdy, rebellious, organic, and relentlessly kinetic

distinctionNotes: Unlike modern polished Drum & Bass, Jungle uses choppy, splintered, vintage acoustic breakbeat loops layered directly over heavy, warm Jamaican dub reggae bass.

name: Breakcore
description: Frenetic, anarchic electronic chaos where classic drum breaks are shattered into millions of microscopic, glitching shards at terrifying speeds. Unpredictable bursts of distorted noise collide with absurd pop melodies and video game sound bites.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Spastic, wildly mutating time signatures and stuttering drum rolls careening at breakneck speeds (180-250+ BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Mangled digital distortion, screaming noise bursts, sudden cut-up classical or pop samples, and crushing gabber kicks
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Screaming punk vocals, absurdly pitched-up anime samples, or glitching vocal screams
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Maniacal, unhinged, rebellious, and overwhelming

distinctionNotes: Unlike Jungle or DnB, Breakcore rejects a steady, danceable groove, deliberately fracturing drum patterns into spastic, irregular, hyper-speed rhythmic breakdowns.

name: Classic Dubstep
description: Dark, cavernous bass music born in late-night London streets, where slow, menacing rimshots echo through freezing, empty urban alleys. The physical focus is entirely on chest-crushing, physical sub-bass tones that vibrate organs without screaming mid-range synths.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Sparse, spacious half-time beat with snapping snare/rimshot on the third count (138-142 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Pure, devastating low-frequency sine rumbles, vast dub delay trails, clicking percussive wooden blocks, and eerie vinyl hiss
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Muted Jamaican dub MC vocal echoes or eerie, distant female vocal fragments
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Brooding, nocturnal, paranoid, and subterranean

distinctionNotes: Unlike Americanized 'Brostep', Classic Dubstep avoids shrieking, aggressive chainsaw synth drops, focusing entirely on pure, meditative sub-bass and eerie dub-reggae acoustic space.

name: Color Bass / Melodic Dubstep
description: Vibrant, iridescent bass music that transforms heavy dubstep drops into exploding rainbows of pitch-tuned synthesizer harmonies and sparkling chord progressions. It blends aggressive physical impact with uplifting, video-game melodies and crystal-clear digital beauty.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Heavy, stomping half-time beat driven by crisp, punchy electronic snares (140-150 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Vocoded bass chords, glistening arpeggios, vocoder-tuned guttural growls, and sparkling chiptune flourishes
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Passionate, soaring pop-EDM vocals singing emotive anthems, or pitched-up vocal chops
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Euphoric, radiant, fantastical, and emotionally charged

distinctionNotes: Unlike raw, monochromatic Dubstep growls, Color Bass runs basslines through melodic vocoders and pitch-resonators to produce glistening, chord-based, iridescent synth textures.

name: Darksynth
description: Aggressive, dystopian electronic music built on fast, distorted 80s synthesizers and heavy, relentless driving beats. Evokes a gritty cyberpunk night chase or horror film.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving, clockwork 4-on-the-floor or fast galloping electro rhythm (120-140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Harsh overdriven synths, buzzsaw basslines, digital distortion, heavy 80s gated drums
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Mostly instrumental; occasional dark samples, robotic vocoders, or distant distorted shouting
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Ominous, aggressive, neon-noir, high-octane horror

distinctionNotes: Unlike standard Synthwave which is nostalgic, bright, and breezy, Darksynth is heavy, abrasive, and borrows heavily from Industrial Metal.

name: Chillwave
description: Hazy, sun-bleached electronic pop drenched in tape saturation, evoking blurred childhood memories of summer vacations through faded Polaroid film. Murmuring, dream-like vocals float over sluggish drum machine loops and shimmering, submerged synthesizers.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Sluggish, relaxed mid-tempo drum machine beats with soft, cushioned impacts (80-95 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Submerged, warbling analog synthesizers, gentle tape hiss, chiming toy-like melodies, and muffled basslines
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Dreamy, heavily reverbed, whispered vocals mixed as an indistinct, ghostly instrument
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Nostalgic, lazy, sun-drenched, and daydream-like

distinctionNotes: Unlike the high-definition neon pulse of Synthwave, Chillwave is slow, lo-fi, woozy, and intentionally degraded with analog tape hiss and muffled textures.

name: Chiptune / 8-Bit
description: High-energy, hyperactive music composed using the primitive, buzzing sound chips of vintage 1980s video game consoles. Its buzzing square waves, rapid-fire arpeggios, and crunchy noise-channel drums create an unmistakable pixelated adventure soundtrack.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Frantic, energetic pulse driven by fast-snapping white-noise drum bursts (130-160 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Buzzy square-wave synths, hollow triangle basslines, rapid machine-gun arpeggios, and lo-fi digital sound FX
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Mostly instrumental; occasional crunchy 8-bit digital voice synthesizers or vocoded squeaks
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Playful, hyperactive, pixelated, and heroic

distinctionNotes: Distinct from other retro-synth styles by its deliberate limitation to the primitive, raw, unpolished audio synthesis hardware of vintage game consoles.

name: Vaporwave
description: Surreal, slowed-down corporate elevator music and smoothed-out 1980s pop hits warped into an eerie, dreamlike consumerist purgatory. It sounds like wandering through an abandoned, marble-tiled shopping mall in 1995 while half-asleep.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Heavily slowed, woozy, drunken drum machine beats that drag and stutter (60-80 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Pitched-down saxophone solos, cheesy corporate synth pads, echoing mall reverbs, and vinyl crackle
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Deeply slowed, pitch-dropped, sluggish pop-star vocals transformed into eerie, androgynous croons
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Haunting, ironic, surreal, and dissociative

distinctionNotes: Unlike Chillwave's sunlit indie nostalgia, Vaporwave specifically uses chopped, screwed, and pitched-down smooth jazz, muzak, and 80s commercial jingles to satirize consumerism.

name: Psytrance
description: High-speed, hypnotic psychedelic dance music driven by an unyielding, rolling bassline that gallops like an electric stallion. Alien squelches, cosmic laser beams, and mind-bending stereo effects swirl relentlessly over a continuous, pounding kick drum.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Continuous, high-velocity 'rolling' bassline that gallops in three-note pulses behind every kick (138-148 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Rubbery modular sweeps, laser-beam synth leads, mind-altering stereo pans, and metallic alien chirps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Hypnotic, mystical vocal chants, philosophical monologue samples, or tribal throat singing
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Mystical, cosmic, manic, and intensely psychedelic

distinctionNotes: Distinguished from other dance music by its relentless, galloping triple-bass bounce ('rolling bass') locked behind every kick drum and its heavy use of alien, psychedelic sound design.

name: Hardstyle
description: Explosive, arena-sized electronic music famous for its massive, violently distorted bass drum that sounds like a roaring hollow gong. Bombastic, emotional stadium synth melodies build into thunderous drops of pure, screaming bass energy.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Very heavy, galloping kick drum with a reversed bass sweep that creates an unyielding 'ta-chew' bounce (150-155 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Massive, screaming distorted kick drums, huge wall-of-sound sawtooth supersaws, and pitch-bent screech leads
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Gravelly, tough-guy spoken hype intros followed by dramatic, soaring stadium vocal anthems
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Heroic, bombastic, aggressive, and overwhelmingly intense

distinctionNotes: Identified instantly by its signature distorted kick drum, which features an overdriven high-pitched attack followed by a roaring, pitch-sliding sub-bass tail.

name: Classic Rock
description: Anthemic, guitar-driven rock music anchored by big, resonant acoustic drums and electric blues riffs that roar through stadium amplifiers. It feels celebratory and rebellious, built for singing along with windows rolled down on an open highway.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving, muscular 4/4 beat anchored by a heavy, resonant acoustic snare drum on counts two and four (110-135 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Crunchy overdriven electric guitars, dynamic walking bass guitar, chiming cymbals, and raw tube amplifier warmth
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Belting, gravelly lead vocals capable of soaring high-pitched screams and bluesy vibrato
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sweaty, triumphant, rebellious, and stadium-sized

distinctionNotes: Unlike Punk Rock's fast amateurism, Classic Rock features virtuoso guitar solos, expansive dynamic arrangements, and a blues-based swing.

name: Grunge
description: Sludgy, brooding rock music that swings violently between quiet, murky verses and explosive, fuzz-drenched choruses. It captures a raw sense of teenage alienation, balancing heavy punk cynicism with lumbering metal riffs.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Lumbering, mid-tempo drum stomp characterized by dramatic explosions from soft hi-hat taps to thrashing cymbals (90-130 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Thick, muddy fuzz-pedal guitar distortion, dirty bass rumbles, and unpolished, bashing drum kits
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Anguished, raspy vocals that shift unpredictably from tired, mumbled laments into throat-tearing screams
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Gloomy, frustrated, unvarnished, and cathartic

distinctionNotes: Unlike Classic Rock's polished bravado, Grunge features dark, self-deprecating lyrics, murky, sludge-distorted guitars, and stark loud-quiet-loud dynamic shifts.

name: Indie Rock
description: Clever, melodic guitar music driven by crisp, nervous rhythms and ringing, unpretentious guitar patterns. It prioritizes emotional vulnerability, quirky lyrical poetry, and catchy, off-kilter hooks over heavy studio polish.

benchmarkTracks.title: I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Peppy, energetic, straight-ahead drum beat with bouncy hi-hat patterns and tight, punchy snare hits (110-140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Jangling, lightly distorted electric guitars, melodic basslines, snappy snare drums, and occasional quirky synthesizers
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Casual, conversational, sometimes crackling or imperfect lead vocals delivering witty, literate lyrics
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Youthful, intellectual, restless, and charmingly unpolished

distinctionNotes: Unlike Grunge or Heavy Metal, Indie Rock avoids crushing, muddy wall-of-sound distortion, utilizing bright, jangly guitars and tidy, infectious melodies.

name: Punk Rock
description: Fast, aggressive, stripped-down rock music played with manic urgency and total disregard for technical perfection. Short, blistering blasts of sound channel pure youthful rebellion, political anger, and chaotic energy.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Frantic, runaway tempo driven by relentless, eighth-note down-picked bass and bashing cymbals (150-200+ BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Raw, buzzing power-chord guitars through cheap amplifiers, clattering drum kits, and distorted, simple basslines
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Snotty, shouted, aggressive lead vocals often accompanied by rowdy, gang-chorus chants
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Confrontational, chaotic, sweaty, and fiercely anti-establishment

distinctionNotes: Unlike Classic Rock, Punk completely rejects virtuosic guitar solos and lengthy songs, condensing tracks into two-minute explosions of raw, three-chord adrenaline.

name: Shoegaze / Dream Pop
description: Lush, overwhelming music where shimmering electric guitars are buried under mountainous waves of reverb, delay, and gentle feedback. Whispered, angelic voices blend into a warm, swirling ocean of sound, making the listener feel weightless.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Sluggish, buried drum pulse that feels like wading through thick, warm water (75-115 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Colossal walls of gliding guitar feedback, tremolo-arm warping, cavernous reverb pedals, and soft, humming basslines
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Ethereal, whispered, breathy voices mixed low beneath the instruments, sounding like an indistinct dream
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Weightless, hypnotic, melancholic, and sensory-overloaded

distinctionNotes: Unlike Indie Rock, Shoegaze completely obliterates clear instrument separation, burying drums and voices beneath a colossal, reverberant wall of swirling guitar noise.

name: Traditional Heavy Metal
description: Theatrical, thunderous heavy music built around twin electric guitars harmonizing over galloping, iron-clad rhythms. Dramatic, operatic vocals soar above songs celebrating dark folklore, fantasy epics, and unstoppable power.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Galloping, martial rhythm driven by tight double-kick accents and pounding basslines (110-145 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Screaming, synchronized dual-guitar harmonies, heavy tube-driven distortion, and bright, slicing guitar solos
sensoryHallmarks.voice: High-pitched, operatic, vibrato-rich theatrical singing capable of glass-shattering screams
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Epic, martial, dramatic, and relentlessly heroic

distinctionNotes: Unlike Thrash or Death Metal, Traditional Heavy Metal utilizes clean, operatic, soaring vocals and classic melodic scales rather than harsh growls or extreme blast-beats.

name: Thrash Metal
description: Blistering, high-velocity metal that marries the dark aggression of heavy metal with the breakneck speed and bite of hardcore punk. Chugging guitar riffs strike with machine-gun precision alongside rapid, barked vocals.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Breakneck, machine-gun rhythmic sprint driven by rapid double-kick drums and lightning skank beats (160-220+ BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Ultra-fast palm-muted 'chugging' guitar riffs with scooped mid-frequencies and chaotic, screeching whammy-bar solos
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Harsh, snarling, aggressively barked or spat vocals delivered at rapid speeds
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Furious, apocalyptic, violent, and adrenaline-charged

distinctionNotes: Unlike Traditional Metal, Thrash strips away melodic twin-guitar sweetness in favor of hyper-speed palm-muted chugging and barked vocal fury.

name: Death Metal
description: Extreme, terrifying sonic violence defined by down-tuned, buzzsaw guitar riffs and inhuman, subterranean guttural roars. Relentless, explosive blast-beat drumming creates an overwhelming physical bludgeoning.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Violent, hyper-speed blast-beats alternating with sudden, sludgy, grinding tempo drops (180-240+ BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Extremely low down-tuned guitars sounding like revving chainsaws, bludgeoning bass, and relentless double-kick artillery
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Deep, inhuman, guttural throat growls and monstrous, unintelligible guttural rasps
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Macabre, suffocating, brutally grotesque, and horrific

distinctionNotes: Distinguished from Thrash and Metalcore by its deep, guttural 'death growl' vocals and continuous, unhinged blast-beat drumming.

name: Metalcore
description: Modern, high-impact heavy music combining ferocious screamed verses with soaring, emotional melodic choruses. Songs build intense kinetic pressure before dropping into massive, slow-motion rhythmic breakdowns designed to move crowds.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving double-kick tempos that abruptly slam into ultra-heavy, half-time syncopated 'breakdowns' (120-150 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Drop-tuned, razor-sharp guitar chugs, soaring melodic dual-guitar leads, and cinematic electronic sub-drops
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Sharp dynamic contrast between harsh, screamed/growled verses and polished, soaring, emotional clean-singing choruses
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Emotionally intense, athletic, cathartic, and modern

distinctionNotes: Identified by its signature 'breakdowns'—sudden, half-time chugging rhythmic stops—and the strict alternating dynamic between screamed verses and clean, catchy pop-metal choruses.

name: Nu-Metal / Alternative Metal
description: Heavy, syncopated rock that fuses downtuned electric guitar riffs with hip-hop bounce, industrial electronics, and raw teenage angst. It prioritizes body-moving groove over fast guitar solos, delivering visceral, unfiltered emotion.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Bouncing, hip-hop-influenced syncopated groove with heavy, deliberate head-nodding impact (85-115 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Sludgy, down-tuned seven-string guitars, percussive slap bass, turntables, and electronic synthesizer glitches
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Eclectic delivery shifting rapidly between rhythmic rapping, agonized whispering, feral screaming, and melodic angst
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Alienated, turbulent, claustrophobic, and raw

distinctionNotes: Unlike Thrash or Traditional Metal, Nu-Metal completely eliminates classic guitar solos in favor of bouncy, hip-hop-style grooves, turntables, and rap-style rhythmic vocals.

name: 90s Boom Bap
description: Gritty, asphalt-flavored hip-hop defined by the crisp, hard crack of an acoustic snare drum and dusty jazz-record samples. Fluid, articulate poets deliver rhythmic rhymes that float over hypnotic, swinging vinyl loops.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Swung, head-nodding beat anchored by a heavy, booming kick drum and a loud, sharp acoustic snare crack (85-95 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Dusty vinyl crackle, chopped-up upright jazz basslines, horn stabs, and warm electric piano loops
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Clear, deeply rhythmic, poetic vocal delivery emphasizing clever rhymes, internal cadences, and street storytelling
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Gritty, urban, nostalgic, and authentic

distinctionNotes: Unlike Modern Trap, Boom Bap uses organic, sampled acoustic drum loops, swinging live-drum feels, and vinyl jazz samples rather than rapid synthesized hi-hats and deep 808 sub-bass.

name: Modern Trap
description: Dark, booming southern hip-hop powered by earth-shaking sub-bass notes and frantic, fluttering metallic hi-hats that skitter like nervous insects. Introspective or boastful lyrics are delivered through sleek, Auto-Tuned vocal flows.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Spacious half-time bounce propelled by frantic, rapid-fire, rolling metallic hi-hat patterns (130-150 BPM, felt at 65-75 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Massive, sustained Roland TR-808 sub-bass booms, crisp digital clap sounds, dark minor-key bell melodies, and eerie synth flutes
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Heavily Auto-Tuned vocal delivery alternating between rhythmic triplet rap flows and hypnotic, melodic croons
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Nocturnal, menacing, luxurious, and drug-hazed

distinctionNotes: Unlike Boom Bap's dusty vinyl drums, Trap relies entirely on electronic 808 sub-bass lines that slide in pitch and skittering, machine-gun digital hi-hat rolls.

name: UK Drill
description: Cold, menacing urban rap driven by wildly sliding, pitch-bending sub-bass notes and an off-balance, skipping drum rhythm. Low-toned, masked narrators deliver clinical, fast-paced street reports over icy, haunting melodies.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Uneven, stumbling, syncopated rhythm where the snare lands with an unexpected skip (140-145 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Wildly pitch-sliding, distorted 808 bass glides, icy piano loops, clicking percussion, and ghostly reverse sounds
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Deep, gravelly, aggressive British/London slang delivered in low, threatening, monotone flows
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Bleak, freezing, tense, and dangerous

distinctionNotes: Distinct from Trap by its off-beat, skipping snare pattern (rather than standard trap claps) and dramatic, pitch-sliding 808 bass glides that leap up and down the musical register.

name: Lo-Fi Hip Hop
description: Cozy, relaxed instrumental beat music colored with intentional imperfections like crackling vinyl, tape wobble, and sleepy jazz piano chords. Evokes studying beside a rain-streaked bedroom window late at night.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Sluggish, unquantized drum machine swing that lags lazily behind the beat (70-85 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Muffled, dusty vinyl surface noise, warbling out-of-tune electric piano keys, soft wooden kicks, and tape flutter
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Predominantly instrumental; occasionally features faint, nostalgic dialogue clips from vintage anime or classic films
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Cozy, studious, comforting, and bittersweet

distinctionNotes: Unlike 90s Boom Bap, Lo-Fi Hip Hop strips away the energetic vocal MC, intentionally degrades sound quality with muffled filters, and maintains a gentle, non-intrusive volume.

name: Cloud Rap / Phonk
description: Dreamy, drug-hazed hip-hop blending weightless, echoing synthesizer clouds with distorted vintage cassette tape samples. Whether floating through ambient soundscapes or ripping through high-speed drift-racing cowbell tracks, it maintains an eerie, otherworldly haze.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Floating, syrupy half-time crawl (in Cloud Rap) or driving, blown-out distorted stomp (in Phonk) (120-145 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Washed-out choir pads, blown-out 808 distortion, repeating tinny cowbell melodies, and lo-fi cassette tape grit
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Mumbled, detached, heavily reverbed singing or chopped, pitch-dropped vintage Memphis rap cassette loops
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Eerie, narcotic, floating, and neon-nocturnal

distinctionNotes: Unlike Modern Trap, Cloud Rap and Phonk feature heavily reverbed, washed-out ethereal ambient textures and pitch-shifted vintage cassette vocal loops.

name: Bebop / Traditional Swing
description: Acrobatic, exhilarating acoustic jazz driven by a shimmering, dancing ride cymbal and walking wooden basslines. Brass instruments trade lightning-fast melodies and complex, dizzying improvisations in an intimate, smoke-filled club.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Fluid, swinging rhythmic skip anchored by a tapping acoustic ride cymbal and a continuous walking upright bass (120-300+ BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm unamplified acoustic double bass, bright brass saxophone and trumpet stabs, and acoustic grand piano runs
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Predominantly instrumental; when vocal, features nimble scat-singing that mimics acoustic instruments
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sophisticated, frantic, virtuosic, and nocturnal

distinctionNotes: Unlike Blues or Soul, Bebop utilizes extremely fast tempos, unpredictable harmonic acrobatics, and complex improvised brass solos rather than repetitive, soulful grooves.

name: Delta / Chicago Blues
description: Earthbound, sorrowful American roots music driven by weeping guitar strings, wailing harmonicas, and raw foot-stomping rhythms. Weathered, heartfelt voices sing of hardship, heartbreak, and resilience through call-and-response laments.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Unhurried, swinging shuffle rhythm following a predictable 12-bar chord cycle (60-100 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Metallic slide guitar strings, weeping bent electric guitar notes, crying harmonicas, and hollow wooden drum thumps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Gravelly, strained, deeply emotional vocal delivery utilizing raw call-and-response shouting
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sorrowful, weathered, earthy, and resilient

distinctionNotes: Unlike Jazz, the Blues is built on simple 12-bar chord structures, bent 'blue notes' that intentionally weep between pitches, and raw storytelling.

name: Motown / Classic Soul
description: Infectious, uplifting rhythm and blues characterized by punchy brass horns, melodic electric bass runs, and driving tambourines. Powerhouse singers deliver church-inspired performances celebrating love and unity.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving, joyful four-beat pulse reinforced by constant tambourine shakes and a lively backbeat (100-125 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Melodic, bubbling electric bass guitar, bright brass sections, vibraphone accents, and crisp handclaps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Virtuosic, impassioned, church-trained lead vocals backed by tight, harmonizing call-and-response choirs
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Joyous, uplifting, romantic, and community-centered

distinctionNotes: Unlike the Blues, Classic Soul is joyous, polished, and radio-ready, propelled by driving tambourines, sophisticated brass sections, and buoyant vocal choruses.

name: Funk
description: Irresistibly groovy, syncopated dance music anchored by a heavy, slapping electric bass and sharp, rhythmic guitar scratches. Everything locks into a deep, sweaty pocket that compels physical movement on the 'one' beat.

benchmarkTracks.title: Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine
Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin)

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Intensely syncopated, rubbery groove that places overwhelming dynamic emphasis on beat 'one' (95-115 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Percussive slapped electric bass, chicken-scratch muted electric guitars, punchy horn blasts, and analog synthesizers
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Rhythmic, spontaneous shouts, grunts, spoken hype calls, and flamboyant communal group singing
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Electrifying, flamboyant, humorous, and unabashedly sweaty

distinctionNotes: Unlike Soul, Funk de-emphasizes romantic vocal melodies in favor of relentless, syncopated rhythm where all instruments—including guitars and voices—act as percussive drums.

name: Neo-Soul
description: Velvety, intimate music blending vintage soul warmth with relaxed, hip-hop drum grooves. Silky, jazz-inflected vocals glide over warm electric piano chords to create a personal, candlelit atmosphere.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Lagging, relaxed drum groove that sits subtly behind the beat with warm, muted acoustic snare hits (75-90 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm Rhodes electric piano chords, round deep bass guitar, muted trumpet mutes, and rich acoustic rimshots
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Silky, breathy, conversational singing rich with complex jazz runs, spoken poetry, and intimate harmonies
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Intimate, sensual, thoughtful, and warm

distinctionNotes: Unlike Classic Soul, Neo-Soul adopts late-90s hip-hop drum sensibilities, lagging behind the beat with muted, cozy acoustic textures and intimate, poetic vocals.

name: Symphonic / Orchestral Classical
description: Grand, sweeping acoustic music performed by dozens of unamplified wooden strings, shining brass horns, and thunderous drums in resonant halls. Its dramatic shifts in volume tell wordless, cinematic stories of human triumph and tragedy.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Flexible, human-led tempo (Rubato) that breathes, accelerates, and halts without a mechanical click
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Bowed acoustic violins, rich cellos, roaring brass horns, woodwind flutes, and booming timpani kettledrums
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Purely instrumental, or accompanied by booming, unamplified operatic choirs singing in Latin or European tongues
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Monumental, architectural, emotionally profound, and timeless

distinctionNotes: Unlike all modern pop genres, Symphonic Classical uses zero electric amplification or steady drum kits, relying on the natural acoustics of large concert halls and large ensembles.

name: Country & Bluegrass
description: Down-home, acoustic string music played on wooden banjos, fiddles, and flat-picked guitars around back porches and barn dances. High, clear vocal harmonies tell timeless tales of mountain life, hard travel, and faith.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Lively train-beat locomotive snare shuffle or steady two-step 'boom-chick' (100-140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Crying pedal steel guitar, country fiddle, bright Telecaster twang, acoustic dreadnought guitar, and five-string banjo
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Twangy, storytelling lead vocals with Southern drawl and high lonesome tenor harmonies
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Dusty honky-tonk bar, rustic front porch, open prairie, or rural dancehall

distinctionNotes: Unlike Country Rock, Bluegrass completely eschews electric guitars and drum kits, relying on acoustic stringed instruments to generate rhythm and melody.

name: Spanish / Flamenco Guitar
description: Fiery, dramatic Spanish acoustic guitar music punctuated by sharp finger-tapping and thunderous hand claps. Rapid nylon-string guitar flourishes weave around deeply emotional vocal cries of love, grief, and pride.

benchmarkTracks.title: Tres Notas Para Decir Te Quiero

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Complex, fluctuating syncopated cycles reinforced by clapping hands (palmas) and stamping wooden heels
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Crisp, bright nylon-string guitar strums (rasgueado), knuckles knocking on wooden soundboards, and castanets
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Strained, passionate, gravelly Andalusian vocal laments (cante) full of raw vibrato and microtonal cries
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Passionate, fiery, tragic, and proudly Andalusian

distinctionNotes: Distinct from classical guitar by its rapid, percussive knuckle-taps on the instrument body, rasgueado finger-strums, and accompaniment by syncopated handclaps.

name: Ambient Neoclassical
description: Intimate, fragile acoustic music where you can hear the creaking wooden pedals of a soft-felted piano and the gentle scrape of a cello bow. It blends classical elegance with ambient silence, creating an intensely personal sanctuary.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Slow, gently drifting, or completely unmetered, moving with the unhurried pace of human breathing (50-70 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Muted 'felted' acoustic piano, close-miked solitary violins, subtle electronic drone washes, and mechanical instrument noises
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Almost exclusively instrumental, preserving absolute stillness
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Introspective, fragile, tenderly melancholic, and peaceful

distinctionNotes: Unlike Symphonic Classical's grand, booming concert halls, Ambient Neoclassical is close-miked, minimalist, quiet, and emphasizes the physical, mechanical noises of the piano itself.

name: Reggae & Dub
description: Hypnotic, sun-warmed Jamaican music where the third beat drops with a heavy drum kick and the rhythm guitar chops on the off-beat. Vast, echoing delay effects wash over deep, vibrating basslines like ocean waves.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Relaxed 'one-drop' rhythm where beat one is empty and the snare/kick lands heavily on beat three (65-80 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Deep, warm electric basslines, short chopped rhythm guitar chords ('skank'), melodica leads, and swirling tape delays
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Spiritual, conscious Jamaican patois singing or chanting, drenched in endless spring reverb and echo
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Spiritual, peaceful, smoky, and deeply grounded

distinctionNotes: Distinguished by its signature 'off-beat' guitar chops and the 'one-drop' drum pulse, which leaves the first beat completely silent while dropping weight onto the third.

name: Bossa Nova
description: Cool, sun-drenched Brazilian music that glides with the elegance of a gentle sea breeze along an open beach. Soft, conversational whispers float over intricate nylon-string guitar chords and lightly brushed drum rhythms.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Gentle, syncopated swaying rhythm played with soft wire brushes on a snare drum (110-130 BPM, felt relaxed)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Delicate, nylon-string acoustic guitar chords, warm upright bass, gentle piano fills, and soft ocean-shaker percussion
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Intimate, quiet, unforced vocal whispers delivered in Portuguese or English without heavy vibrato
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Romantic, breezy, sophisticated, and sun-lit

distinctionNotes: Unlike fast, festive Samba, Bossa Nova reduces percussion to a whisper, favoring intimate nylon-string jazz chords and breathy, soft singing.

name: Reggaeton / Latin Trap
description: High-energy, body-moving Caribbean urban music propelled by an unmistakable, stomping 'boom-ch-boom-chick' drum groove. Charismatic vocalists deliver rapid-fire Spanish rhymes and catchy, party-starting choruses.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: The signature, hard-hitting 'Dem Bow' syncopated drum rhythm: a heavy kick followed by two syncopated snare snaps (90-100 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Sharp electronic timbales, deep synthetic sub-bass kicks, synthetic brass stabs, and tropical synth melodies
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Energetic, rhythmic Spanish vocal delivery moving between fast-talking rap verses and Auto-Tuned sung hooks
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sensual, festive, sun-soaked, and relentlessly danceable

distinctionNotes: Instantly recognized by the inescapable Caribbean 'Dem Bow' rhythm—a mechanical 'boom-ch-boom-chick' pattern that underpins virtually every track.

name: Afrobeats
description: Buoyant, infectious West African pop music built on rolling polyrhythmic drum patterns and bright, sunny melodies. Sweet, silky vocals weave in and out of warm horn lines and clean guitar riffs, celebrating romance and triumph.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Syncopated, undulating West African drum bounce that makes the body sway continuously (98-108 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm electronic keyboard chords, clean plucked African guitar licks, wooden log-percussion taps, and lush brass stabs
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Melodic, buoyant, sing-along vocal deliveries shifting seamlessly between English, Nigerian Pidgin, and Yoruba
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Joyful, celebratory, breezy, and warm

distinctionNotes: Unlike Reggaeton's rigid Dem Bow beat, Afrobeats uses flowing, rolling West African polyrhythms, clean highlife guitars, and sunny melodic pop hooks.

name: Amapiano
description: Deep, hypnotic South African house music driven by a signature rattling shaker and a resonant, subterranean 'log drum' that punches and slides in the low frequencies. Mellow, jazzy piano chords float across an unhurried, magnetic township groove.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Unhurried, low-slung house pulse with a crisp off-beat shaker and sudden, percussive log-drum bursts (110-116 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm, jazzy Rhodes piano chords, ticking shakers, airy flutes, and the iconic, metallic, pitching 'log drum' bass kick
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Soulful, breathy vocal melodies and repetitive, rhythmic call-and-response vocal chants in Zulu and Xhosa
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Spiritual, hypnotic, sophisticated, and deeply rhythmic

distinctionNotes: Distinguished from standard Deep House by its lower tempo (112 BPM), continuous rolling shaker percussion, and the prominent, pitched, metallic South African 'log drum'.

name: Progressive House
description: Epic, melodic club music built around patient emotional builds, soaring synthesizer hooks, and clean four-on-the-floor drops.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Steady, punchy four-on-the-floor kick with driving offbeat open hi-hats (126-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Layered melodic synthesizer plucks, euphoric supersaw leads, white noise sweeps, and deep rolling bass
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Soaring, clean, emotional pop-style vocal anthems or purely instrumental builds
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Massive festival mainstage euphoria, laser-lit arenas, and emotional climaxes

distinctionNotes: Unlike Tech House's sterile minimalism, Progressive House is melodically maximalist with long emotional chord progressions and dramatic buildups.

name: Electro House
description: High-voltage, abrasive dance music featuring grinding sawtooth basslines, robotic vocal glitches, and massive distorted drops.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Heavy, pounding four-on-the-floor kick with hard, snappy snare claps on beats two and four (126-130 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Buzzing, overdriven distorted saw-wave basslines, pitch-bent screech leads, and chopped vocal glitch snippets
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Robotic vocoder phrases, playful hype one-liners, or aggressive shouted vocals
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Adrenaline-fueled, gritty, robotic, and electrifying

distinctionNotes: Unlike standard House's warm soulful pianos, Electro House relies on aggressive distortion, abrasive buzzing basslines, and razor-sharp digital edges.

name: Tropical House
description: Breezy, relaxed dance music featuring sunny pan flutes, bright marimbas, and smooth melodic hooks that evoke a beach sunset.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Gentle, unhurried four-on-the-floor thump with a relaxed, swaying shuffle (100-115 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Synthetic pan flutes, wooden marimba plucks, bright acoustic guitar strums, and warm rounded sub-bass
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Airy, clean, smooth pop singing delivering gentle, romantic melodies
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sunny, beachside, breezy, relaxed, and sun-drenched

distinctionNotes: Unlike club-focused Tech or Deep House, Tropical House runs at a much slower tempo (100-114 BPM) and prominently features acoustic marimbas and pan flutes.

name: Afro House
description: Hypnotic, percussion-heavy house music that interlocks warm electronic four-on-the-floor kicks with rich West and South African hand drumming.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Steady, rolling four-on-the-floor kick surrounded by dense polyrhythmic hand shakers and congas (120-125 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Deep warm sub-bass, organic kalimbas, ethnic wooden shakers, and lush atmospheric synthesizer chords
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Chanted African vocal harmonies, spiritual mantras, or soulful English melodies
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Spiritual, earthy, hypnotic, and deeply rhythmic

distinctionNotes: Unlike Tech House's sterile mechanical percussion, Afro House is saturated with organic, acoustic wooden hand percussion and spiritual warmth.

name: Bass House
description: Gritty, aggressive hybrid of UK garage, dubstep, and four-on-the-floor house, characterized by massive metallic wobbles and pitch-shifting bass drops.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Punchy, heavy four-on-the-floor kick with hard snapping claps (126-128 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Metallic FM-synth wobbles, gritty distorted reese bass growls, and subterranean sub-pressure
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Chopped hip-hop vocal stabs, pitched-down one-liners, or ragga hype shouts
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Dark, aggressive, high-octane club energy

distinctionNotes: Unlike Tech House, Bass House features massive, aggressive metallic wobbles derived directly from Dubstep and UK Garage bass design.

name: Dub Techno
description: Deeply hypnotic, cavernous techno washed in infinite tape-delay echo trails, filtered chord stabs, and vinyl hiss.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Muffled, warm, subterranean four-on-the-floor kick drum (118-124 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Cavernous tape-delay echoes, filtered minor chord stabs trailing into infinite reverb, and soft analog tape hiss
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Instrumental; occasional ghostly, distant, un-decipherable vocal fragments
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Cavernous, meditative, subterranean, oceanic, and deeply immersive

distinctionNotes: Unlike Peak-Time Techno's hard abrasive kicks, Dub Techno is soft, cavernous, and bathed in endless dub reggae-style tape echoes.

name: Acid Techno
description: Relentless, hard-edged underground techno driven by screaming, squelching Roland TB-303 synthesizer lines and distorted kicks.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Pounding, unyielding four-on-the-floor kick drum (135-145 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Screaming, resonant Roland TB-303 acid squelch, metallic open hi-hats, and industrial distortion
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Almost exclusively instrumental
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sweaty, underground illegal warehouse rave, psychedelic, and relentless

distinctionNotes: Unlike Acid House, Acid Techno is much faster (135-145 BPM), much harder, and trades soulful pianos for industrial mechanical aggression.

name: Hard Techno
description: Brutal, high-velocity techno built from distorted industrial kicks, relentless mechanical repetition, and furious energy.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Sledgehammer four-on-the-floor kick drum pounding at relentless speeds (145-160 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Heavily saturated, distorted kick drums, industrial metal percussion, and screaming modular synthesizer noise
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Instrumental or harsh, shouted punk-style vocal snippets
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Apocalyptic, furious, visceral moshpit energy inside a concrete bunker

distinctionNotes: Unlike standard Techno (125-132 BPM), Hard Techno pushes speeds to 150+ BPM with extreme distortion and visceral, violent physical impact.

name: Hypertechno
description: High-energy commercial techno characterized by rapid 140-155 BPM rolling basslines, prominent vocal hooks, and high-gloss mainstage rave euphoria.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Rapid 140-155 BPM four-on-the-floor beat with rolling offbeat bassline
sensoryHallmarks.sound: High-gloss electronic production, punchy modern kicks, heavy subbass, and bright rave synths
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Prominent pitched vocal hooks, fast spoken vocal chops, or autotuned vocal refrains
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: High-voltage festival rave euphoria and contagious mainstage bounce

distinctionNotes: Unlike underground Hard Techno which is dark, violent, and distorted, Hypertechno is glossy, uplifting, and dominated by catchy vocal refrains and eurodance-tinged rave hooks.

name: Trance
description: Euphoric, emotional electronic music driven by a steady four-on-the-floor pulse, soaring arpeggios, and dramatic cinematic buildups.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Relentless, driving four-on-the-floor kick with sharp offbeat hi-hats (135-140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Soaring supersaw synth chords, glistening arpeggios, rolling basslines, and white noise riser sweeps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Ethereal, soaring female vocal anthems or purely instrumental emotional themes
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Transcendental, euphoric, emotional, and arena-filling

distinctionNotes: Unlike Techno, which is repetitive and mechanical, Trance is hyper-melodic, emotional, and centered around massive soaring breakdowns.

name: Uplifting Trance
description: The emotional peak of trance music, featuring hyper-fast rolling bass, massive church-like breakdowns, and triumphant supersaw climaxes.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving, fast four-on-the-floor kick with rolling 138-142 BPM basslines
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Enormous detuned supersaw synth leads, grand piano breakdown solos, and lush orchestral string pads
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Angelic, soaring, high-register vocal performances singing themes of love and liberation
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Transcendental euphoria, hands-in-the-air festival arena ecstacy

distinctionNotes: Unlike Psytrance's alien modular squelches, Uplifting Trance is defined by massive emotional orchestral breakdowns and soaring major-key supersaws.

name: Jump Up DnB
description: High-energy, playful drum and bass characterized by cartoonish screeching bass synths, rolling two-step breakbeats, and hype MC vocals.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Rapid, punchy two-step drum pattern at blistering speed (174-178 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: High-pitched, screeching 'foghorn' and laser synth melodies, bouncy sub-bass, and crisp snappy snares
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Energetic live MC hype toasting and crowd chants
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Chaotic, sweaty, rowdy, and athletic rave energy

distinctionNotes: Unlike Neurofunk's dark dystopian sci-fi growls, Jump Up features cartoonish, high-pitched screeching synth hooks designed for instant hype.

name: Brostep
description: Abrasive, adrenaline-charged bass music characterized by aggressive robotic screech leads, snarling growls, and crushing half-time drops.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Heavy half-time beat with colossal snare crack on beat three (140-150 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Harsh, snarling metallic growls, screeching vocoder shrieks, and subterranean sub-bass impacts
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Quirky pop-culture speech samples, aggressive screamed pre-drop chants, or pitch-shifted hooks
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Intense, chaotic, headbanging, and explosive festival energy

distinctionNotes: Unlike Classic Dubstep's deep, quiet, spacious sub-bass rumbles, Brostep is aggressively loud, mid-range heavy, and full of metallic robotic growls.

name: UK Garage / Future Garage
description: Sensual, swinging urban electronic music featuring syncopated skipping 2-step beats, warm pitched vocal chops, and deep rubbery bass.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Shuffling, swung 2-step syncopated beat with skipped snare hits (130-138 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warm Rhodes electric keys, vinyl surface rain crackle, filtered pitched vocal snippets, and deep rounded basslines
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Melancholic, chopped R&B vocal samples pitched up or down into emotional textures
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Nocturnal, rainy, urban, reflective, and deeply soulful

distinctionNotes: Unlike four-on-the-floor House, UK Garage uses a syncopated, skipping 2-step rhythm where the second kick drum is displaced.

name: Gabber / Hardcore Techno
description: Furious, unrelenting rave music driven by ultra-fast, heavily overdriven distorted kicks, screeching industrial stabs, and raw energy.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Ferocious four-on-the-floor distorted kick pounding at extreme speeds (160-200 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Extreme square-wave kick distortion, roaring sawtooth synthesizer shrieks, and industrial noise
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Aggressive shouted or pitched-down Dutch/English rave mantras
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Manic, furious, strobe-lit, and physically exhausting

distinctionNotes: Unlike Hardstyle (150 BPM with pitch-bending reverse bass), Gabber is much faster (160-200 BPM) and uses abrasive, squared-off distorted kick drums.

name: IDM / Glitch
description: Intricate, cerebral electronic music featuring complex algorithmic drum programming, warm analog synths, and micro-sound glitch textures.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Unpredictable, shifting, asymmetric breakbeats and micro-percussion (variable BPM, often 90-140 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Warped analog synthesizers, digital clicks and cuts, tape-degraded poly-pads, and micro-sampled noise
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Rare; heavily processed, pitch-bent vocal fragments or vocoders
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Cerebral, headphone-focused, nostalgic, melancholic, or alien

distinctionNotes: Unlike functional club music designed for dancefloors, IDM is designed for attentive home headphone listening with complex asymmetric rhythms.

name: Psychedelic Rock
description: Mind-bending rock music featuring swirling phasing effects, feedback-drenched guitar solos, modal jamming, and surreal lyrics.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving 4/4 rock beat with loose, swinging cymbals and fluid transitions
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Wah-wah electric guitars, lush flanger/phaser effects, sitar textures, and Hammond organ sweeps
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Dreamy, echoing melodic singing or impassioned blues-rock shouting
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Trippy, disorienting, expansive, colorful, and surreal

distinctionNotes: Unlike Classic Rock's straight riffs, Psychedelic Rock uses heavy studio audio effects (flangers, delays, reverse tape) to simulate altered states.

name: Black Metal
description: Dark, icy extreme metal characterized by relentless blast beats, buzzing tremolo-picked guitar walls, shrieked vocals, and raw lo-fi production.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Relentless, high-velocity blast beats and fast galloping double-kicks
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Raw, buzzing walls of tremolo-picked electric guitar chords recorded with cold, thin, distorted lo-fi fidelity
sensoryHallmarks.voice: High-pitched, rasping, agonized shrieks and feral hisses
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Bleak, freezing, nocturnal, medieval, and misanthropic

distinctionNotes: Unlike Death Metal's low-tuned chugging riffs and deep guttural throat growls, Black Metal uses thin buzzing tremolo picking and high-pitched shrieks.

name: Traditional Country & Honky-Tonk
description: Heartfelt, storytelling music from rural America, driven by the crying slides of the pedal steel guitar, twangy Telecasters, and two-step rhythms.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Brisk locomotive two-step 'boom-chick' rhythm or walking bass shuffle (100-130 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Crying, pitch-sliding pedal steel guitar, bright Telecaster twang, acoustic dreadnought guitar, and fiddle
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Rich, resonant baritone or twangy tenor vocals with clear Southern diction and emotional vibrato
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Neon-lit roadside honky-tonk, sawdust dancehall, open prairie highway

distinctionNotes: Unlike Funk or Rock, Country is defined by narrative storytelling, the unmistakable crying glide of the pedal steel guitar, and alternating root-fifth bass.

name: Salsa & Mambo
description: Irresistible, fiery Latin dance music powered by interlocking congas, timbales, walking piano montunos, and blazing brass horns.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Driving, complex syncopated clave rhythm with rapid conga slaps and cowbell accents (180-220 BPM dance tempo)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Syncopated acoustic piano montunos, explosive brass horns (trumpets, trombones), and rich Afro-Cuban percussion
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Passionate Spanish vocal improvisation (sonero) with vibrant call-and-response group choruses
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Sun-drenched, celebratory, fiery, and deeply communal

distinctionNotes: Unlike Reggaeton's modern electronic dembow kick, Salsa is completely acoustic and live, driven by the traditional two-three clave pattern and live brass.

name: Dark Ambient
description: Claustrophobic, ominous soundscapes built from low-frequency subterranean drones, distant metallic echoes, and total absence of rhythm.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Complete absence of drums, pulse, or meter (unmetered dark space)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Subterranean sub-bass rumbles, distant echoing metal clangs, deep low-pass drone textures
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Instrumental with occasional ghostly, distant whispering
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Ominous, terrifying, subterranean, claustrophobic, and apocalyptic

distinctionNotes: Unlike standard Ambient, Dark Ambient is menacing, dissonant, and devoid of warm relaxation.

name: Trip Hop / Downtempo
description: Dark, smoky, slow-motion urban beats fusing dusty 90s hip-hop breakbeats, warm jazz organs, and sensual cinematic vocals.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Slow, heavy, swung hip-hop breakbeat (75-90 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Dusty vinyl crackle, warm Fender Rhodes chords, deep upright or sub-bass, and cinematic strings
sensoryHallmarks.voice: Sensual, melancholic, breathy female or male singing
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Nocturnal, smoky lounge, cinematic, melancholic, and mysterious

distinctionNotes: Unlike pure Ambient, Trip Hop is heavily rhythmic with slow, swung, dusty hip-hop drum loops.

name: Happy Hardcore / UK Hardcore
description: Manic, euphoric rave music driven by blistering 170 BPM four-on-the-floor beats, pitch-shifted female pop vocals, and joyful piano riffs.

sensoryHallmarks.pulse: Manic, unyielding four-on-the-floor kick at blistering speed (165-175 BPM)
sensoryHallmarks.sound: Bright bouncy synth stabs, joyful acoustic piano riffs, and snappy off-beat hi-hats
sensoryHallmarks.voice: High-pitched chipmunk-style or hyper-clean female vocal singing euphoric anthems
sensoryHallmarks.atmosphere: Transcendental, childish, joyous, euphoric, and strobe-lit

distinctionNotes: Unlike dark Gabber or aggressive Hardstyle, Happy Hardcore is unabashedly joyful, fast (170 BPM), and driven by bright piano chords.
